answer: Sequential Work Inlet. New agents enter through a single queue where each identity must complete a fixed batch of useful computation before acting; throughput is capped per epoch, so enrolling many identities just spreads the same work thinner. The queue is a narrow inlet, and surplus identities wait in a holding lagoon until their batch clears. An attacker flooding registrations pushes their own entry time toward the nadir, paying real compute and calendar delay per identity. Cost: one full work batch plus queue latency per sybil.
